original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
imaṃ vivasvate yogaṃ proktavānahamavyayam|
vivasvān manave prāha manurikṣvākave'bravīt
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa (the Blessed Lord) says: I declared this imperishable (avyaya) yoga to Vivasvat; Vivasvat told it to Manu; Manu told it to Ikṣvāku.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'This yoga' points back to the teaching already given (chs. 2–3). The text says only 'Manu'; the commentators identify him as Vivasvat's son (Vaivasvata Manu).

original.text:
evaṃ paramparāprāptamimaṃ rājarṣayo viduḥ|
sa kāleneha mahatā yogo naṣṭaḥ parantapa
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Received in this way through succession (paramparā), it was known by the royal sages (rājarṣi). Through a great lapse of time that yoga was lost here, scorcher of foes.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
sa evāyaṃ mayā te'dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ|
bhakto'si me sakhā ceti rahasyaṃ hyetaduttamam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: That same ancient (purātana) yoga I have declared to you today, because you are my devotee (bhakta) and my friend (sakhā); for this is the highest secret (rahasya).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The stated reason for imparting the teaching (being devotee and friend) marks the recipient's qualification.

original.text:
aparaṃ bhavato janma paraṃ janma vivasvataḥ|
kathametadvijānīyāṃ tvamādau proktavāniti
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Arjuna says: Your birth was later, Vivasvat's birth earlier. How am I to understand that you declared it in the beginning?
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cārjuna|
tānyahaṃ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṃ vettha parantapa
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Many births (janma) of mine have passed, and of yours too, Arjuna. I know them all; you do not know them, scorcher of foes.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
ajo'pi sannavyayātmā bhūtānāmīśvaro'pi san|
prakṛtiṃ svāmadhiṣṭhāya saṃbhavāmyātmamāyayā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Though I am unborn (aja), with an imperishable self, and though I am the lord (īśvara) of beings, taking my stand on (adhiṣṭhāya) my own nature (prakṛti) I come into being (saṃbhavāmi) through my own māyā (ātmamāyā).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The word avatāra does not occur in the Gītā; the verbs are saṃbhavāmi (4.6, 4.8) and sṛjāmi (4.7). Commentators divide on 'ātmamāyā' (e.g. the Lord's power of appearance in Śaṅkara; his own will or knowledge in Rāmānuja) and on whether 'prakṛti' here is material nature under his control or his own essential nature.

original.text:
yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata|
abhyutthānamadharmasya tadā''tmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Whenever there is a decline (glāni) of dharma and a rise of adharma, Bhārata, then I send myself forth (sṛjāmi).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām|
dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya saṃbhavāmi yuge yuge
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: For the protection of the good (sādhu), for the destruction of evil-doers, and for the firm establishing of dharma, I come into being age after age (yuge yuge).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
janma karma ca me divyamevaṃ yo vetti tattvataḥ|
tyaktvā dehaṃ punarjanma naiti māmeti so'rjuna
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Whoever knows in truth (tattvataḥ) that my birth and action (janma, karma) are divine (divya) in this way does not, on leaving the body, go to rebirth (punarjanma); he comes to me, Arjuna.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
vītarāgabhayakrodhā manmayā māmupāśritāḥ|
bahavo jñānatapasā pūtā madbhāvamāgatāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Freed from passion (rāga), fear and anger, absorbed in me (manmaya), taking refuge in me, many, purified by the austerity of knowledge (jñāna-tapas), have come to my state of being (madbhāva).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'jñānatapasā' can be read 'by knowledge as austerity' or 'by knowledge and austerity'. Commentators differ on whether 'madbhāva' means identity with the Lord's being or attaining a nature like his.

original.text:
ye yathā māṃ prapadyante tāṃstathaiva bhajāmyaham|
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: In whatever way people resort to me (prapadyante), in just that way I respond to them (bhajāmi). People follow my path (vartman) in every way, Pārtha.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The second line repeats 3.23b word for word, where it means that people follow the Lord's example; here commentators read it either so or as 'whatever path people follow is mine'. 'bhajāmi' = I reciprocate / favour / apportion (to them).

original.text:
kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇāṃ siddhiṃ yajanta iha devatāḥ|
kṣipraṃ hi mānuṣe loke siddhirbhavati karmajā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Desiring the success (siddhi) of their actions, people here sacrifice to the deities (devatā); for in the human world success born of action comes quickly.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
cāturvarṇyaṃ mayā sṛṣṭaṃ guṇakarmavibhāgaśaḥ|
tasya kartāramapi māṃ viddhyakartāramavyayam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: The fourfold order of classes (cāturvarṇya) was created by me according to the division of qualities (guṇa) and actions (karma). Though I am its maker, know me as the imperishable non-doer (akartṛ).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The verse itself does not say whether class is fixed by birth; commentators read 'guṇa-karma-vibhāga' through the guṇas predominating in each class and the duties assigned to it (cf. 18.41–44).

original.text:
na māṃ karmāṇi limpanti na me karmaphale spṛhā|
iti māṃ yo'bhijānāti karmabhirna sa badhyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Actions do not stain (limpanti) me; I have no longing for the fruit of action (karmaphala). Whoever knows me thus is not bound by actions.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
evaṃ jñātvā kṛtaṃ karma pūrvairapi mumukṣubhiḥ|
kuru karmaiva tasmāttvaṃ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṃ kṛtam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Knowing this, even the ancients who sought liberation (mumukṣu) performed action. Therefore you too should simply perform action, as it was performed by the ancients of old.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
kiṃ karma kimakarmeti kavayo'pyatra mohitāḥ|
tatte karma pravakṣyāmi yajjñātvā mokṣyase'śubhāt
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: 'What is action (karma)? What is inaction (akarma)?' — even sages (kavi) are bewildered about this. I will declare to you that action, knowing which you will be released from the inauspicious (aśubha).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
karmaṇo hyapi boddhavyaṃ boddhavyaṃ ca vikarmaṇaḥ|
akarmaṇaśca boddhavyaṃ gahanā karmaṇo gatiḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: For one must understand action (karma), one must understand vikarma, and one must understand inaction (akarma): deep (gahana) is the course of action.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The verse does not define vikarma; commentators divide between 'prohibited/wrong action' (e.g. Śaṅkara) and 'action of special or varied kinds'.

original.text:
karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśyedakarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ|
sa buddhimān manuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ kṛtsnakarmakṛt
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: One who sees inaction (akarma) in action and action in inaction is wise (buddhimān) among humans; he is yoked (yukta) and a doer of all action (kṛtsna-karma-kṛt).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Commentators explain the paradox very differently (e.g. the actionless self amid the body's activity; unattached action as effectively non-action; abstention itself as a kind of action). The paraphrase keeps the text's paradox without choosing.

original.text:
yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāmasaṅkalpavarjitāḥ|
jñānāgnidagdhakarmāṇaṃ tamāhuḥ paṇḍitaṃ budhāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: One whose every undertaking (samārambha) is free of desire (kāma) and of purposive intention (saṅkalpa), whose actions have been burned up by the fire of knowledge (jñānāgni) — him the wise call learned (paṇḍita).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
tyaktvā karmaphalāsaṅgaṃ nityatṛpto nirāśrayaḥ|
karmaṇyabhipravṛtto'pi naiva kiñcitkaroti saḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Having abandoned attachment (āsaṅga) to the fruit of action, ever content (nitya-tṛpta), depending on nothing (nirāśraya), though fully engaged in action he does nothing at all.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
nirāśīryatacittātmā tyaktasarvaparigrahaḥ|
śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Without expectations (nirāśīḥ), with mind and self restrained, having given up every possession (parigraha), performing merely bodily action (śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma), he incurs no fault (kilbiṣa).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma' is read either as action done merely for the body's maintenance (e.g. Śaṅkara) or as action done by the body alone (without inner involvement).

original.text:
yadṛcchālābhasantuṣṭo dvandvātīto vimatsaraḥ|
samaḥ siddhāvasiddhau ca kṛtvāpi na nibadhyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Content with whatever comes by chance (yadṛcchā-lābha), gone beyond the pairs of opposites (dvandva), free of envy (matsara), the same (sama) in success and failure — even though he acts he is not bound.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
gatasaṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthitacetasaḥ|
yajñāyācarataḥ karma samagraṃ pravilīyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: For one whose attachment (saṅga) is gone, who is free (mukta), whose mind is established in knowledge, and who acts for the sake of sacrifice (yajña), action dissolves entirely (samagraṃ pravilīyate).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
brahmārpaṇaṃ brahmahavirbrahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam|
brahmaiva tena gantavyaṃ brahmakarmasamādhinā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: The offering (arpaṇa) is Brahman, the oblation (havis) is Brahman, poured by Brahman into the fire that is Brahman; Brahman alone is to be reached by one whose concentration (samādhi) is on action as Brahman (brahma-karma).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'arpaṇa' may denote the instrument of offering (e.g. the ladle) or the act of offering; 'brahma-karma-samādhinā' can be read 'by one absorbed in action that is Brahman' or 'by one who sees Brahman in action'. 'samādhi' here is not given the technical sense of Yoga Sūtra 1–3.

original.text:
daivamevāpare yajñaṃ yoginaḥ paryupāsate|
brahmāgnāvapare yajñaṃ yajñenaivopajuhvati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Some yogins attend (paryupāsate) to sacrifice (yajña) directed to the gods (daiva) alone; others offer sacrifice by sacrifice itself into the fire of Brahman.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The second line is obscure; commentators take it as offering the self (or sacrifice as such) into Brahman, i.e. seeing the sacrifice as Brahman.

original.text:
śrotrādīnīndriyāṇyanye saṃyamāgniṣu juhvati|
śabdādīnviṣayānanya indriyāgniṣu juhvati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Others offer the senses, hearing and the rest, into the fires of restraint (saṃyama); others offer the sense-objects (viṣaya), sound and the rest, into the fires of the senses.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'saṃyama' here is restraint of the senses, not the technical saṃyama (dhāraṇā-dhyāna-samādhi) of Yoga Sūtra 3.4. Commentators take the second line as enjoying sense-objects without attachment.

original.text:
sarvāṇīndriyakarmāṇi prāṇakarmāṇi cāpare|
ātmasaṃyamayogāgnau juhvati jñānadīpite
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Others offer all the actions of the senses and the actions of the vital breath (prāṇa) into the fire of the yoga of self-restraint (ātma-saṃyama-yoga), kindled by knowledge.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
dravyayajñāstapoyajñā yogayajñāstathāpare|
svādhyāyajñānayajñāśca yatayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Others likewise sacrifice with material things (dravya-yajña), with austerity (tapo-yajña), with yoga (yoga-yajña); and ascetics (yati) of strict vows (saṃśita-vrata) sacrifice with recitation (svādhyāya) and with knowledge (jñāna-yajña).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'svādhyāya-jñāna-yajñāḥ' can be one compound ('whose sacrifice is the knowledge gained by recitation') or two sacrifices (recitation, and knowledge).

original.text:
apāne juhvati prāṇa prāṇe'pānaṃ tathā'pare|
prāṇāpānagatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāmaparāyaṇāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Others, intent on breath-regulation (prāṇāyāma), offer prāṇa into apāna and apāna into prāṇa, restraining the courses of prāṇa and apāna.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The segment reads 'prāṇa' where the usual text has 'prāṇaṃ'. The verse does not say which movement (in- or out-breath) each name denotes; commentators differ.

original.text:
apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇānprāṇeṣu juhvati|
sarve'pyete yajñavido yajñakṣapitakalmaṣāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Others, regulated in food (niyatāhāra), offer the vital breaths (prāṇa) into the vital breaths. All these are knowers of sacrifice, whose impurities (kalmaṣa) are destroyed by sacrifice.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yajñaśiṣṭāmṛtabhujo yānti brahma sanātanam|
nāyaṃ loko'styayajñasya kuto़'nyaḥ kurusattama
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Eating the nectar (amṛta) that is the remainder of sacrifice (yajña-śiṣṭa), they go to the eternal (sanātana) Brahman. This world is not for one who does not sacrifice — how then the other, best of Kurus?
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
evaṃ bahuvidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe|
karmajānviddhi tānsarvānevaṃ jñātvā vimokṣyase
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text; source repository under the Unlicense)

paraphrase: Thus sacrifices of many kinds are spread out in the mouth of Brahman (brahmaṇo mukhe). Know them all to be born of action (karmaja); knowing thus you will be released.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'In the mouth of Brahman' is not explained in the text; commentators read it as 'in the Veda' (the sacrifices being set out there) or as 'offered into Brahman (as into a mouth or fire)'.

original.text:

sarvaṃ karmākhilaṃ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate

paraphrase: Chapter 4 (Kṛṣṇa to Arjuna, with one question from Arjuna) moves as follows. (1) 4.1–3: the imperishable yoga was taught by Kṛṣṇa to Vivasvat, passed to Manu and Ikṣvāku and known by the royal sages through succession, was lost over time, and is now re-told to Arjuna as devotee and friend. (2) 4.4–10: Arjuna asks how Kṛṣṇa could have taught Vivasvat; Kṛṣṇa answers that he and Arjuna have had many births which he alone knows; though unborn and lord of beings he comes into being by his own māyā whenever dharma declines, to protect the good and establish dharma; knowing his divine birth and action frees one from rebirth, and many purified by knowledge have reached his state. (3) 4.11–15: he responds to people as they approach him; people sacrifice to deities for quick success; he made the fourfold class-order yet is a non-doer, unstained by action, and the ancients seeking liberation acted knowing this — so Arjuna should act. (4) 4.16–23: the difficult analysis of action, wrong action (vikarma) and inaction; the wise one sees inaction in action, acts without desire or attachment to fruit, his actions burnt by the fire of knowledge, and is not bound. (5) 4.24–32: sacrifice (yajña) extended: every factor of the offering is Brahman, and a catalogue of sacrifices (to the gods, into Brahman, senses into restraint, objects into senses, breath, material goods, austerity, yoga, recitation and knowledge, breath-regulation, regulated food), all born of action. (6) 4.33–42: the sacrifice of knowledge is superior and all action culminates in knowledge; knowledge is to be learnt from truth-seeing knowers by prostration, questioning and service; it is a raft, a fire, the supreme purifier, gained by faith and sense-control and leading to peace; the doubter perishes; Arjuna is to cut his doubt with the sword of knowledge, resort to yoga and stand up. Purpose, as the chapter presents it: to ground the teaching of action in an ancient divine transmission and in the Lord's own nature, and to show action performed with knowledge, as sacrifice, as not binding.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Colophon titles for this chapter vary between editions and are not part of the segment file; they are not used here.

paraphrase: Chapter 5 (Kṛṣṇa to Arjuna, opened by Arjuna's question) moves as follows. (1) 5.1: Arjuna asks which is better, renunciation of actions (saṃnyāsa) or yoga. (2) 5.2–6: both lead to the highest good, but the yoga of action is superior; the constant renouncer is one who neither hates nor craves; only the childish separate Sāṃkhya and Yoga, which reach the same place; renunciation is hard to attain without yoga. (3) 5.7–12: the one yoked in yoga, whose self has become the self of all beings, acts without being stained; the knower thinks 'I do nothing', the senses move among their objects; placing actions in Brahman and giving up attachment he is untouched like a lotus leaf; yogins act for self-purification; giving up the fruit brings lasting peace, while desire binds. (4) 5.13–17: the embodied one, having renounced actions mentally, dwells in the nine-gated city neither acting nor causing action; the lord does not create agency or its fruits — svabhāva acts; knowledge is covered by ignorance, and when ignorance is destroyed knowledge lights up the highest; those devoted to That go to non-return. (5) 5.18–26: the learned see all beings equally; those established in sameness conquer the world here, for Brahman is the same; the knower of Brahman is unmoved by pleasant and unpleasant, finds happiness within; contact-born pleasures are wombs of sorrow; withstanding desire and anger, with inner happiness, delight and light, the yogin becomes Brahman and attains brahma-nirvāṇa. (6) 5.27–28: a brief instruction (external contacts shut out, gaze between the brows, prāṇa and apāna made even) describing the sage who is forever free. (7) 5.29: knowing Kṛṣṇa as enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, great lord of all worlds and friend of all beings, one attains peace. Purpose, as the chapter presents it: to answer the question of renunciation versus the yoga of action by showing that true renunciation is inward and that disciplined action leads to the same goal, brahma-nirvāṇa and peace.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Colophon titles for this chapter vary between editions and are not part of the segment file; they are not used here.

paraphrase: Chapter 6 (Kṛṣṇa to Arjuna, with Arjuna's two questions) moves as follows. (1) 6.1–4: the renouncer and the yogin are one who does required action without depending on its fruit, not one who merely abandons fires and rites; no one becomes a yogin without renouncing intention (saṅkalpa); for one wishing to ascend to yoga action is the means, for one who has ascended calm (śama) is the means, and ascent is defined as non-attachment to sense-objects and actions. (2) 6.5–9: one must raise oneself by oneself — the self is its own friend or enemy; the self-conquered, tranquil yogin is steady in all pairs of opposites, satisfied with knowledge, and equal toward all. (3) 6.10–17: instruction in meditation — solitude, a clean firm seat, one-pointed mind, erect posture, gaze toward the nose-tip, celibacy, mind fixed on Kṛṣṇa — leading to peace culminating in nirvāṇa; moderation in food, recreation, sleep and waking. (4) 6.18–23: the state of yoga: the controlled mind resting in the self like a lamp in a windless place; the mind stilled, the self seen by the self, boundless happiness beyond the senses, unshaken by sorrow — this is yoga, the unyoking from union with sorrow, to be practised with resolve. (5) 6.24–28: method: giving up desires born of intention, gradually coming to rest with a firm intellect, thinking of nothing, bringing back the wandering mind; the result is supreme happiness, becoming Brahman, contact with Brahman. (6) 6.29–32: the yogin sees the self in all beings and all beings in the self, sees Kṛṣṇa everywhere, worships him in all beings established in oneness, and regards others' pleasure and pain as his own. (7) 6.33–36: Arjuna objects that the mind is too restless; Kṛṣṇa grants it but says it is held by practice (abhyāsa) and dispassion (vairāgya). (8) 6.37–45: Arjuna asks the fate of one who has faith but falls from yoga; Kṛṣṇa answers that no doer of good perishes — he dwells in meritorious worlds, is reborn among the pure or among yogins, regains his former understanding, is carried by former practice, and, perfected through many births, reaches the highest goal. (9) 6.46–47: the yogin is greater than ascetics, knowers and ritualists — be a yogin; and among yogins the one who worships Kṛṣṇa with faith and inner self fixed on him is the most yoked. Purpose, as the chapter presents it: to set out the discipline of meditative yoga (its prerequisites, method, state and result), to reassure about failure in it, and to crown it with faith-filled worship of the Lord.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
